sample_unit: guideline PECO questions (20 challenges: with and without data prompting)

links.outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT recommendations with ESCMID brain abscess guideline and patient hazard
links.effect: Without data prompting 70% of answers very similar to guideline, no patient hazard in differing answers; with data input, fewer correct answers including two recommendations directly contradicting guideline with possible patient hazard.
links.quote: Data input slightly improved the clarity of ChatGPT's recommendations, but, however, led to less correct answers including two recommendations that directly contradicted the guideline, being associated with the possibility of a hazard to the patient.

links.outcome: Whether LLM performance on guideline questions reflects safe clinical competence
links.effect: ChatGPT gave recommendations for 17 of 20 challenges, but single responses could possibly harm patients; expert committee remains necessary.
links.quote: Nevertheless, single responses could possibly harm the patients.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating ChatGPT on ESCMID guideline questions with and without providing specific study evidence data (prompting with source literature).
